title: POC scoping - Private networking & data residency - Luminex Health
summary: Redwood AE/SE and Luminex stakeholders scoped a Private networking POC: choose between VPC peering and PrivateLink, confirm EU data residency, map egress constraints (firewall/NAT/Proxy), define workloads for benchmarks and success criteria, and agree on a 3-week pilot + security review path.
transcript:
Header: 2026-12-01 14:00 PST | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Sara Lee (PM, Luminex), Raj Patel (Infra), Tom Nguyen (Security)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we got the agenda out, quick intros — I'm Maya, AE on Redwood.
[00:07] Daniel Ortiz: hi all, daniel SE here, i'll lead the technical part of the POC scoping.
[00:12] Sara Lee: Sara here, product, we're looking to run a private networking POC for sensitive patient-note processing, so we care a lot about data residency and egress.
[00:21] Raj Patel: Raj - infra. we've got an on-prem core and AWS in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 for europe, want to keep eu data in eu.
[00:29] Tom Nguyen: Tom, security. SOC 2 is in place but we need KMS integration and audit logs visible in our SIEM.
[00:36] Maya Chen: Great. high-level: Redwood offers private deployment options — VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and a Private control plane depending on your requirements. We'll cover network patterns, egress, and the benchmarks you'll need.
[00:48] Sara Lee: Our timeline is tight — board wants demo and preliminary numbers in three weeks. is that realistic?
[00:54] Daniel Ortiz: it's tight but doable if we scope a focused benchmark: 1) 10k daily inference sessions, 2) burst concurrency of ~150 requests, 3) p95 latency target 200-300ms for small context use cases. we can show throughput and cost per 1M tokens.
[01:12] Raj Patel: quick question — for PrivateLink do we need to open up any egress to the internet or can traffic stay in our VPCs?
[01:19] Daniel Ortiz: PrivateLink terminates in your VPC — traffic doesn't traverse the public internet to Redwood's service endpoints; you'll create VPC endpoints in your account. VPC peering is also possible but for multi-account and region setups PrivateLink is usually simpler.
[01:32] Tom Nguyen: if we use PrivateLink, can we still have the control plane communicate out for monitoring? we need audit logs forwarded to our splunk cluster.
[01:40] Maya Chen: yes, logs can be forwarded; for Private deployments we offer options: collect logs to an S3 bucket in your account, or push to your SIEM via our secure delivery. we'll provide the integration doc.
[01:52] Sara Lee: region question — EU data must remain in eu-west-1 per legal. can we pin the inference instance and KV cache to eu-west-1 for the POC?
[01:59] Daniel Ortiz: absolutely. you can pin model instances to eu-west-1 and enforce routing policies so any EU customer traffic stays in-region. if you want HA across zones we'll place across two AZs in eu-west-1.
[02:10] Raj Patel: network egress: our infra team has strict egress rules via a NAT/proxy. we can't allow arbitrary outbound IPs. what IP ranges will Redwood need whitelisted?
[02:19] Maya Chen: we'll share a minimal set of egress addresses — for PrivateLink there's typically no egress, but for control-plane callbacks and metrics there are specific IP ranges and hostnames. we'll send a CIDR list and options for static IPs via NAT gateway.
[02:32] Tom Nguyen: also need KMS/HSM integration — can keys stay in our KMS? we can't have customer data keys managed externally.
[02:40] Daniel Ortiz: yes you can use your AWS KMS to encrypt model runtime artifacts and logs. our Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS. we'll include a sample key policy.
[02:51] Sara Lee: success criteria from our side: 1) benchmarks meet latency and throughput targets, 2) no data leaves eu region during inference, 3) security signoff (logs, KMS, SSO), and 4) cost estimate within threshold.
[03:05] Maya Chen: sounds good. to add: we want to validate model quality regression — we'll run eval prompts to check responses against baseline. that's part of the POC pass/fail.
[03:16] Raj Patel: workload sizing — our initial workload is about 10k sessions/day with avg session length 120 tokens in, 150 tokens out. estimate concurrency: typical peak 150 concurrent small requests, and a separate embedding batch job that will run nightly processing about 500k records.
[03:33] Daniel Ortiz: for the conversational workload that maps to roughly 2-3 dedicated gpus if we use a mid-size quantized model (e.g., 13B q4). embedding night batch could be run on a separate dedicated pool with autoscale for cost. we'll prepare a sizing matrix with models and GPU types.
[03:49] Sara Lee: we also need an SLA during the pilot — even if it's not formal, we need expected uptime and p95 latency targets.
[03:56] Maya Chen: for Dedicated/private pilots we aim to meet latency SLOs in our runbook; for hosted we publish performance profiles. we'll include an SLA addendum for the pilot.
[04:05] Tom Nguyen: auditing — we need request-level audit logs with request IDs, timestamps, and redactions of PHI. can Redwood redact or mask outputs at rest?
[04:15] Daniel Ortiz: we can tag transcripts and store them in your encrypted bucket; PII redaction is something we'll apply via post-processing or via customer-side redaction before storage. we'll include patterns for redaction in the guide.
[04:28] [short silence / notes being typed]
[04:35] Maya Chen: okay practical steps — daniel will define the benchmark matrix: concurrency shapes, token distributions, model variants, and measurement scripts. sara/raj will provide network constraints, whitelist requirements, and a sample dataset for quality evals (de-identified).
[04:50] Sara Lee: we have a sample of 5k de-identified notes ready, can share after data handling agreement is signed.
[04:56] Raj Patel: timeline — we can allocate infra people for the first week of December. do you need anything ahead of time?
[05:03] Daniel Ortiz: network ACLs and any egress proxy config upfront. also, if you choose PrivateLink, provide AWS account IDs and VPC IDs for endpoint creation.
[05:12] Tom Nguyen: on compliance docs, we need SOC 2 artifacts and a security questionnaire answer sheet.
[05:17] Maya Chen: I'll follow up with the security pack; we keep SOC 2 and ISO snippets in the doc, and we'll fill the RFP/RA questions.
[05:24] Sara Lee: benchmarks — can we set the pass criteria numerically? e.g., p95 < 300ms, throughput > X tokens/s?
[05:31] Daniel Ortiz: yes, propose p95 < 300ms for single-turn small context in eu-west-1, and a throughput baseline of 200 tokens/s per GPU for the chosen quantized model — exact numbers will be in the matrix.
[05:44] Raj Patel: for embeddings batch, we need predictable cost. can you estimate cost per 1M embeddings?
[05:50] Maya Chen: we'll include cost estimates across model sizes; early ballpark for a 13B quantized model is X USD per 1M tokens -- we'll provide a clearer table.
[05:59] Sara Lee: who will run the actual benchmark? Redwood or Luminex?
[06:03] Daniel Ortiz: we can run an initial Redwood-hosted run inside your private network via PrivateLink endpoints, or we can hand off the scripts and you run them. recommended: Redwood runs initial baseline to eliminate environment differences, then you run a final verification.
[06:17] Tom Nguyen: network security check — will you provide a terraform module or CloudFormation for endpoint setup?
[06:23] Daniel Ortiz: yes we have example Terraform modules for creating PrivateLink endpoints and peering configs; we'll attach them.
[06:30] Maya Chen: okay let's capture explicit next steps and owners.
[06:35] [10:00 minute mark — cross-checking calendar items]
[06:40] Sara Lee: also need to confirm data residency on backups and logs — backups must stay in eu region and not replicate to us-east.
[06:50] Daniel Ortiz: we can configure storage buckets in your account in eu-west-1 and disable cross-region replication.
[06:56] Raj Patel: what about egress for model downloads or updates? we will be behind strict proxy; will the runtime pull model artifacts or will Redwood push them?
[07:05] Maya Chen: for Private deployments we can push model artifacts via a pre-signed S3 transfer into your account, or have the runtime pull from a signed endpoint through your NAT. both work, pushing is more controlled.
[07:18] Tom Nguyen: audit requirement: every inference must have a trace id and an operator field. can Redwood include these in headers?
[07:25] Daniel Ortiz: yes we support passing custom metadata in request headers and we'll include trace_id in logs.
[07:32] Sara Lee: onboarding docs — can you share a checklist for infra, security, and product so we know exactly what's needed for week 1?
[07:39] Maya Chen: absolutely — we'll send a POC runbook: network checklist, credentials, sample scripts, benchmark matrix, and security pack.
[07:47] [pauses — people typing]
[07:55] Daniel Ortiz: small note: if you expect frequent small requests, consider prefix caching/KV cache to cut latency and cost. we'll show caching impact in the benchmark.
[08:05] Raj Patel: last question — if we need on-prem later, how different is the setup?
[08:10] Maya Chen: on-prem is similar conceptually but we deploy a private control plane in your network, plus connectors for logging and KMS. it's a bigger integration but doable once pilot succeeds.
[08:21] Sara Lee: okay can we recap the success criteria and timeline?
[08:25] Maya Chen: recap: success criteria = (1) p95 latency < 300ms for target workload, (2) no data leaves eu region, (3) security signoff (KMS, logs, SSO), (4) model quality meets your eval thresholds, (5) cost estimate within agreed threshold. timeline: immediate kick-off, Redwood delivers runbook & whitelist by 2026-12-03, initial baseline Redwood-run benchmark week of 12/7, customer verification week of 12/14, security signoff by 12/18, pilot wrap-up/decide next steps by 12/21.
[08:58] Tom Nguyen: those dates align with internal deadlines, we'll try to expedite the security questionnaire.
[09:04] Raj Patel: we'll share VPC IDs and proxy configs by EOD 12/2.
[09:09] Maya Chen: Perfect. i'll follow up with the POC runbook and the security pack after this call. thanks everyone.
[09:16] Sara Lee: thanks.
[09:18] [call ends]
